content: The Kentucky School for the Deaf was established due to the efforts of General Elias Barbee, whose daughter, Lucy, was deaf. General Barbee introduced a bill to the Kentucky Assembly, which led to the school being located in Danville under the administration of the Centre College Board of Trustees. In 1825, John Adamson Jacobs became the principal of the school. Since its founding, the school has had 14 superintendents, and it is currently led by Dr. Harvey Jay Corson. One of the campus's most historically significant structures, Jacobs Hall, is the oldest surviving building and has been designated as a National Historic Landmark. The school's athletic teams are known as the Colonels. While their overall success has been moderate, they have achieved at least one championship in high school 8-man football.
